title: Cube-block parity of the odd inverse candidate is a new Diophantine invariant
statement: The parity of the unique inverse candidate k=ceil(y^{2/3}) is a modular/Diophantine law of the cube-block residue r=y-m^3 (m=icbrt(y)), invisible from floor(x^{3/2}) mod 2, and an infinite flight is an infinite nested sequence of those cubic-lane conditions.
counterexamples: Type-2 y in B_m = [m^3,(m+1)^3) are exactly {T(x): x odd in [m^2,(m+1)^2)}; identity holds on m<=40 and {50,80,100}
offsets are not an AP at n_type2>=3 (m=5 offsets 0,15,31,47,64,82 have four gaps); no deciding residue modulo 2,3,4,8,16,m,2m+1
m=1 pair {1,5} is r≡0 (mod 4) in a 7-point block and is not a law
backward Type-2 spines descend (max depth 3 on y<=200); named images T(3),T(37),T(365),T(761) have depth 1 and die at a Type 0 occupant
forward continuation requires the image itself to be odd: landing parity, already CLOSE as odd_landing_sets / odd_tower
mathematical_domain: Juggler descent-free flights / odd inverse cells
notes: Phase 0 only. Inverse candidate is the Type-2 occupant of J-odd-pred-empty-cube. Nested cubic conditions are a direction error. No odd-landing rerun, no odd-tower rerun, no Lean, no Paper A, no ledger theorem row. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: identity m<=40 and {50,80,100}; residue/AP hunt on those blocks; named hits {3,37,365,761}; backward nest Type-2 y<=200
